subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub adopt a public acceptability rule for agent-directed SKILL.md/README instructions, and where should that rule live relative to acceptable usage, capability manifests, and review-pipeline guidance?
rationale: The RFC sets a marketplace trust and security boundary rather than fixing broken current behavior; current docs only cover adjacent execution, declaration, and audit concepts, so automation cannot choose the policy line safely.

options.title: Accept as policy work
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold into related RFCs
options.body: Treat this boundary as dependent on the declared-capability and cross-asset review RFCs, then decide the public policy and manifest/review behavior together.

options.title: Keep internal for now
options.body: Leave the boundary as internal ClawScan/moderator judgment and decline to publish a submitter-facing rule until more cases accumulate.

recommendation.title: Accept as policy work
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest routing signal across CODEOWNERS-listed security docs, scanner prompt, moderation paths, and adjacent current policy text.
